ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: How Fashion Items Got Their Names

fullPassage:
How Fashion Items Got Their Names

Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers transformed this functional design into luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there are other fashion items with interesting stories about how they got their names.

Sneak Up in Sneakers

You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for everyday activities or sports. They are a type of athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for physical activities and sports. So, why are they called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived from the term "to sneak up."

Due to the fact that sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they make little noise when people walk. This allows people who are wearing them to sneak up on others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly sneak up on your friends and surprise them.

Blue Jeans from Genoa

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a modification of Gênes, the French name of the Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods throughout Europe, particularly in England and France. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue jeans in English.

A Man in a Tuxedo in Tuxedo Park

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in New York. In the late 19th century, men usually wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park. The male guests who stayed there were fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear the same style. Later, more people asked their tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in Tuxedo Park." At first, this style of jacket was considered less formal than one with long tails. As more and more men wore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the longer version. Now men's formal wear is the tuxedo. Isn't it ironic that the tuxedo was not originally considered very formal, but now it is the most formal clothing men wear?

Flip-flops, Flip-flop

On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear simple shoes with a band across the top of the foot and between the big toe and second toe. Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they have such a long history, they have different names all around the world. The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the name of the shoes, flip-flops.

Whatever origins these fashion items have, they are being worn by more and more people in various places around the world. Why don't you look for other fashion items that have as interesting name origins as those introduced here?

questions.passage: Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name (A)[indicates / contradicts], the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers (B)[transformed / maintained] this functional design into luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there are other fashion items with (C)[interesting / boring] stories about how they got their names.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이름이 나타내듯이 점프수트는 비행기에서 뛰어내리는 의복으로 시작했다. 디자이너들이 이 기능적 디자인을 고급스러운 패션 아이템으로 변형시켰다. 흥미로운 이야기들이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① indicates — transformed — interesting
❌ ② contradicts — transformed — interesting
❌ ③ indicates — maintained — boring
❌ ④ contradicts — maintained — interesting
✅ (A) indicates: '나타내다'. contradicts(모순되다)는 이름과 기원의 관계를 정반대로 표현. ✅ (B) transformed: '변형시키다'. maintained(유지하다)는 변화 맥락과 반대. ✅ (C) interesting: '흥미로운'. boring(지루한)은 원문과 반대.
det.tip: indicate(나타내다) vs contradict(모순되다). transform(변형시키다) vs maintain(유지하다).

questions.passage: You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for everyday activities or sports. They are a type of athletic shoe designed (A)[specifically / accidentally] to be worn for physical activities and sports. The name "sneakers" is (B)[derived / separated] from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they make little noise when people walk. This allows people who are wearing them to sneak up on others. However, with sneakers, you can (C)[quietly / loudly] sneak up on your friends and surprise them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 운동화는 신체 활동을 위해 특별히 설계된 신발이다. 이름은 'to sneak up'에서 유래했다. 고무 밑창 덕분에 조용히 다가갈 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① accidentally — derived — quietly
❌ ② specifically — separated — loudly
✅ ③ specifically — derived — quietly
❌ ④ specifically — derived — loudly
✅ (A) specifically: '특별히'. accidentally(우연히)는 의도적 설계와 반대. ✅ (B) derived: 'be derived from'은 '~에서 유래하다'. separated(분리되다)는 어원 맥락과 무관. ✅ (C) quietly: '조용히'. loudly(시끄럽게)는 몰래 다가가는 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: be derived from = '~에서 유래하다'. specifically(특별히) vs accidentally(우연히).

questions.passage: Blue Jeans from Genoa Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a (A)[modification / imitation] of Gênes, the French name of the Italian city of Genoa. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods (B)[throughout / outside] Europe, particularly in England and France. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally (C)[suited / opposed] to making tough work clothes. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: jean이라는 단어는 Gênes의 변형이다. 제노바 상인들은 유럽 전역에서 상품을 거래했다. 튼튼한 작업복을 만드는 데 이상적으로 적합한 면직물이었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① imitation — throughout — suited
✅ ② modification — throughout — suited
❌ ③ modification — outside — suited
❌ ④ modification — throughout — opposed
✅ (A) modification: '변형'. imitation(모방)은 단어 변화 맥락과 맞지 않음. ✅ (B) throughout: '전역에'. outside(밖에서)는 유럽 내 무역이라는 맥락과 반대. ✅ (C) suited: 'suited to'는 '~에 적합한'. opposed(반대하는)는 의미 반대.
det.tip: modification(변형): 원래 단어가 변하여 새 단어가 됨. suited to(~에 적합한) vs opposed to(~에 반대하는).

questions.passage: Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers ①<u>transformed</u> this functional design into ②<u>luxurious</u> women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world. You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for everyday activities or sports. They are a type of athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for ③<u>physical</u> activities and sports. The name "sneakers" is ④<u>separated</u> from the term "to sneak up."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.analysis: ✅ ①transformed: 기능적 디자인을 변형 — 원문 그대로. ✅ ②luxurious: 고급스러운 패션 아이템 — 원문 그대로. ✅ ③physical: 신체 활동 — 원문 그대로. ❌ ④separated: 원문은 derived(유래했다). separated(분리되다)는 어원 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: derived from(~에서 유래한) ↔ separated from(~에서 분리된). 어원 설명에서는 derived가 적절.

questions.passage: People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. det.korean: 처음에 이 스타일의 재킷은 긴 꼬리가 달린 것보다 덜(less) 격식 있는 것으로 여겨졌다. more는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①formal: 격식 있는 행사 — 원문 그대로. ✅ ②fascinated: 매료되었다 — 원문 그대로. ❌ ③more: 원문은 less formal. 처음에는 덜 격식 있게 여겨졌다가 나중에 가장 격식 있는 옷이 됨. ✅ ④replaced: 대체했다 — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: less formal(덜 격식적인) ↔ more formal(더 격식적인). 문맥상 처음에는 덜 격식적이었다는 역설이 핵심.

questions.passage: On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear simple shoes with a band across the top of the foot and between the big toe and second toe. Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they have such a long history, they have different names all around the world. The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the __________ of the shoes, flip-flops.
